claude.rationale: gap_45=1: the customer-facing furnace assets (ASFs) at the Mesa facility were directed toward disposition to satisfy Apple's $439M secured claim, while the sapphire materials operation was set to wind down and the sapphire growth IP was retained by the registrant — the product-layer assets crossed toward disposition without the producing/delivery processes moving coherently alongside. The gap is contractually bridged by the subordinated DIP financing facility (up to $150M) using those ASFs as collateral, hence gap_mitigated=yes. gap_56=uncertain: the slice describes disposition of furnace assets and wind-down of an operation but does not document whether operational processes were re-engineered or transferred relative to the people/organization running them at closing.

gemini.rationale: The settlement agreement structured a wind-down of the sapphire materials business while retaining specialty materials and ASF sales, with Mesa facility ASFs sold to satisfy Apple's claim. No structural mismatch between product and process (gap_45 = 0) or process and organization (gap_56 = 0) was documented at closing.

openai.rationale: The slice states that the customer-facing ASFs at the Mesa facility were directed toward sale to satisfy Apple's secured claim, while GT retained the sapphire-growth intellectual property and only part of its product portfolio was implicated. No associated production or delivery processes are documented as transferring with those furnace assets, establishing gap_45. No operational processes are documented as transferring or being re-engineered without the organization or personnel that operated them, so gap_56 is coded 0; the DIP financing arrangement provided collateral-based financing rather than a transitional-services or operating agreement.
